Strategic Alignment (excerpt) Source: page 4 • Sustainable and responsible operations, balancing innovation with fiscal responsibility, privacy, and environmental considerations Privacy Source: pages 7–8 How the District Uses AI Safely and Responsibly The district may use artificial intelligence tools to support learning, communication, and day-to-day operations. When we do, protecting student and staff information is a top priority. Below is a clear explanation of how we safeguard data and respect privacy. Protecting Student and Staff Information When AI tools are used, the district takes steps to protect students, staff, and district information from misuse, leaks, or unauthorized access. Any use of AI must follow existing district technology and privacy rules, as well as federal and state privacy laws, including laws that protect student education records. Overview: Principle 4, Privacy and Data Security Source: PDF pages 1–2 4. Privacy and Data Security Student and staff data must be protected. No personally identifiable information … including Individual Education Plans (IEP), 504 Plans, … contents, student performance data, or health information — should be entered into any AI tool. Exceptions may be granted for specific tools that the District AI Committee and Technology Department have expressly approved for Personally Identifiable Information use, provided a signed Student Data Privacy Agreement is in place before any such data is entered. Tool selection was based on criteria such as: • Compliance approval with the NYCPS Enterprise Request Management Application (ERMA) data privacy and security review process. How Teachers and School Staff Members May Use AI (excerpt) Source: web page, section 'How Teachers and School Staff Members May Use AI' Teachers and other school staff members may continue using AI for instructional planning and operational tasks, subject to existing requirements, including the NYCPS Enterprise Request Management Application (ERMA) data privacy and security approval process, and NYCPS procurement rules. Additionally, AI may not be used for grading, behavior monitoring, or for placement, promotion, graduation, and other decisions about students.
